verses.text: A good name is better than fine perfume, and the day of death is better than the day of birth.
It is better to go to a house where people are mourning than to a house where people are feasting. For death is the end of everyone, and the living should take this to heart.
Sorrow is better than laughter, because a sad face can make the heart better.
The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of fun.
It is better to listen to the correction of a wise person than to listen to the songs of fools.
Like the crackling of thorns burning under a pot, so is the laughter of a fool. This too is meaningless.
Surely cheating people makes a wise person foolish, and a bribe ruins the mind.
The end of a thing is better than its beginning. Being patient is better than being proud.
Do not be quick to get angry, for anger lives in the heart of fools.
Do not say, "Why were the old days better than these?" It is not wise to ask that.
Wisdom is as good as an inheritance. Yes, it is even better, for all who live under the sun.
For wisdom protects, just as money protects. But the advantage of knowledge is this: wisdom keeps alive the one who has it.
Think about what God has done. Who can make straight what he has made crooked?
When times are good, be happy. When times are bad, think about this: God has made the one as well as the other, so that people cannot find out what will come after them.
In my meaningless life I have seen all this: a righteous person dying even though they do right, and a wicked person living long even though they do evil.
Do not be too righteous, and do not make yourself too wise. Why destroy yourself?
Do not be too wicked, and do not be a fool. Why die before your time?
It is good to hold on to the one warning and not let go of the other. For whoever has respect for God will avoid all extremes.
Wisdom makes one wise person stronger than ten rulers in a city.
Surely there is no one on earth who is righteous, who always does good and never sins.
Also, do not pay attention to every word people say, or you may hear your servant cursing you.
For you know in your heart that many times you yourself have cursed others too.
I tested all this with wisdom. I said, "I will be wise," but it was far beyond me.
Whatever exists is far off and very deep. Who can find it out?
So I turned my heart to understand, to explore, and to search for wisdom and the meaning of things, and to understand that wickedness is stupid and that foolishness is madness.
I found something more bitter than death: the woman whose heart is a trap and a net, and whose hands are chains. The one who pleases God will escape her, but the sinner will be caught by her.
"Look," says the Teacher, "this is what I have found, adding one thing to another to find the answer,
which I am still searching for but have not found. I found one upright man among a thousand, but I have not found one woman among all of them.
Look, this is the only thing I have found: God made people upright, but they have gone looking for many schemes."
